questions.text: The word "technology" comes from which two Greek words?
questions.explanation: Technology comes from the Greek words techne and logos.

questions.text: Match each term from the etymology of "technology" to its meaning.
allChoices: Art, skill, craft, or the way a thing is gained
The word or utterance by which inward thought is expressed
"Systematic treatment" of grammar or an art
A discourse or technical treatise on an art
The actual application of the mechanical and industrial arts and sciences

pairs.match: Art, skill, craft, or the way a thing is gained
The word or utterance by which inward thought is expressed
"Systematic treatment" of grammar or an art
A discourse or technical treatise on an art
The actual application of the mechanical and industrial arts and sciences

questions.explanation: Techne is art/skill/craft and logos is the word that expresses inward thought. The Greek technologia meant a systematic treatment of grammar or an art. In the 17th century English "technology" meant a technical treatise on an art. By the 19th century it meant the actual application of those arts and sciences.

questions.text: Technology is the making, modification, usage, and knowledge of tools, machines, techniques, crafts, systems, and methods of organization in order to:
options: Solve a problem or improve a pre-existing solution
Reduce the cost of raw materials
questions.explanation: The definition ends with "in order to solve a problem, improve a pre-existing solution."

questions.text: According to the module, entrepreneurship is the practice of:
options: Managing employees on behalf of an owner
Converting good ideas to something profitable
Providing capital in exchange for future gains
Holding two or more jobs at the same time
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurship is "the practice of converting good ideas to something profitable." The other options describe management, investing, and moonlighting.

questions.text: Entrepreneurship is a process of identifying and starting a business venture, sourcing and organizing the required ___, and taking both the risks and rewards associated with the venture.
questions.explanation: The definition reads: "...sourcing and organizing the required resources, and taking both the risks and rewards associated with the venture."

questions.text: Technopreneurship is simply:
options: Working two jobs, one of them in IT
questions.explanation: The module defines it as "simply entrepreneurship in a technology intensive context."

questions.text: Technopreneurship is the process of merging technology and entrepreneurial ___ and skills.
questions.explanation: "It is the process of merging technology and entrepreneurial talent and skills."

questions.text: Which of these IT jobs has the highest annual salary ceiling in the list of high-paying jobs in the PH?
questions.explanation: The list shows DevOps Engineer at P850,000 to P1,500,000 annually. Software Engineer tops out at P1,200,000, Data Scientist at P1,200,000, and Network Security Engineer at about P1,000,000.

questions.text: According to the 2023-2024 figures in the module, how many out of 10 graduates apply in a company after graduation?
questions.explanation: 7 out of 10 graduates apply in a company, 1 out of 10 puts up their own business, and the remainder stay at home.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as PROS of being a business owner (as opposed to an employee)?
questions.explanation: The business-owner pros are flexible work hours, diverse learning experience, and a greater sense of personal satisfaction. A guaranteed paycheck is listed as a pro of being an employee.

questions.text: According to the module, in the short term a business owner will always make more money than an employee.
questions.explanation: In the short term the employee makes more money. In the long term the business owner has the potential to make more money and reap additional benefits.

questions.text: What mainly distinguishes an entrepreneur from management?
options: The entrepreneur is the owner who bears both profit and loss, while management runs the company through administrative functions
The entrepreneur only provides capital, while management invents the product
The entrepreneur works for a salary, while management owns the company
There is no difference; the two terms are interchangeable
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur owns the company and bears both profit and loss. Management operates and runs the company with the help of various administrative functions.

questions.text: How does an investor differ from an entrepreneur?
options: An investor invents or innovates a good or service and accepts all the risk of failure
An investor provides capital to a business in exchange for the expectation of future gains and profits
An investor runs the company's day-to-day administrative functions
An investor holds two or more jobs at the same time
questions.explanation: An investor is a person or group that provides capital in exchange for expected future gains and profits. It is the entrepreneur who launches the company to invent or innovate.

questions.text: What is moonlighting?
options: Holding down two or more jobs at the same time
Managing a company on behalf of its owner
questions.explanation: Moonlighting is holding two or more jobs at once, usually one primary income source plus a side gig or freelance work.

questions.text: According to the module, how does a technopreneur differ from an entrepreneur?
options: A technopreneur starts out with nothing but an "idea" and defies existing practices and systems
A technopreneur only invests money in tech companies
A technopreneur avoids risk and relies on proven business models
A technopreneur is always a large corporation
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur identifies an opportunity and converts it into a product or service. A technopreneur starts out with just an idea, defies existing practices, and thinks of doing things differently.

questions.text: Technopreneurship involves a coming together of people who are:
options: Passionate, with an appetite for calculated risk
questions.explanation: The module lists people who are intelligent, driven, creative, tech-savvy, passionate and have an appetite for calculated risk. Risk-averse is the opposite of that.

questions.text: For a technopreneur, it is not as much about the money as it is about:
options: The affirmation that the "idea" is a worthy one and that it works
Avoiding the 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. routine
questions.explanation: The module says it is about the affirmation that the idea is worthy and works, and the idea needs to work for the greater common good.

questions.text: For a technopreneur's idea to be worthwhile, it must become a global blockbuster.
questions.explanation: The module says the idea needs to work for the greater common good, and that it doesn't need to be a global blockbuster.

questions.text: More often than not, technopreneurship begins with:
options: A new technology, then looks for a customer
The customer experience, then works backward to the technology that provides it
A copy of an existing competitor's product
questions.explanation: Technopreneurship begins with the customer experience and works backward to arrive at the technology to provide that experience.

questions.text: The Philippine government defines the size of a small business based on:
options: Annual profit and number of branches
Number of customers and years in operation
questions.explanation: The government categorizes a business by how much it owns (asset size) and how many people work for it (employment size).

questions.text: Match each business category to its asset size.
questions.explanation: By asset size: Micro is up to P3M, Small is P3,000,001 to P15M, Medium is P15,000,001 to P100M, and Large is above P100M.

questions.text: Match each business category to its employment size.
questions.explanation: By employment size: Micro is 1 to 9, Small is 10 to 99, Medium is 100 to 199, and Large is more than 200 employees.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as ADVANTAGES of a small business?
options: Can easily modify products to address market demand and preferences
Lack of skill in marketing planning and market studies
Can easily adjust production, personnel and other systems in times of economic crisis
questions.explanation: Product flexibility, faster communication, and the ability to adjust in an economic crisis are all listed advantages. Lack of marketing skills is a disadvantage.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as DISADVANTAGES of a small business?
options: Lack of skills in marketing planning and doing market studies
Hardly undertaking promotional activities such as media advertising
Control and administration centralized in the hands of the owner-manager
questions.explanation: Weak marketing skills, little promotion, and centralized control by the owner-manager are listed disadvantages. Faster communication is an advantage.

questions.text: Many small businesses may fail because of the lack of a workable and realistic ___ plan.
questions.explanation: Disadvantage #6 reads: "Many small businesses may fail because of lack of workable and realistic financial plan."

questions.text: According to DTI, which of the following are NON-human resources that an entrepreneur puts together?
questions.explanation: Human resources are workers, managers, customers, and suppliers. Non-human resources are land and building, money, machines, materials, and methods or processes.

questions.text: How does DTI describe the risk-taking of an entrepreneur?
options: Betting money on chance outcomes like a gambler or speculator
Putting resources together to realize business objectives even though the result is uncertain
Avoiding any investment until success is guaranteed
Passing all losses on to investors
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs take risks "not just in the way gamblers and speculators do," but by putting resources together to realize business objectives whose result is uncertain.

questions.text: Small entrepreneurs are often called the "backbone of the economy" or the "___ of growth."
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs are called the "backbone of the economy" or "the engine of growth" because they help build the nation.

questions.text: Match each role of the entrepreneur in society to the description or example given in the module.
allChoices: Hiring people so they can feed their families and pay income taxes
Faster stoves, microwave ovens and pressure cookers making cooking easier
Locating in the provinces to spread development and slow migration to the metropolis
Making handicrafts and computer casings out of pandan, rattan and bamboo
Taxes, duties and licenses paying for roads, schools, and medical services

pairs.match: Hiring people so they can feed their families and pay income taxes
Faster stoves, microwave ovens and pressure cookers making cooking easier

pairs.term: Contribute to a wider distribution of income
pairs.match: Locating in the provinces to spread development and slow migration to the metropolis
Making handicrafts and computer casings out of pandan, rattan and bamboo
Taxes, duties and licenses paying for roads, schools, and medical services

questions.explanation: These are the five societal roles (4a-4e) from DTI. Employment: hiring. Quality of life: cooking innovations. Wider income distribution: locating in rural areas. National productivity: local materials such as bamboo. Social benefits: government revenue from taxes, duties and licenses.

questions.text: Bamboo being used as computer casing is given as an example of which role of the entrepreneur?
questions.explanation: Bamboo computer casing, a part of the green computing scheme, illustrates putting locally abundant natural resources to good use.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as RISKS of being an entrepreneur?
questions.explanation: The risks are the risk of failure, long hours of hard work, and unwanted responsibilities. Being your own boss is listed as a reward, along with making money, expressing creativity, and feeling fulfilled.

questions.text: Which environment can a small business owner actually control, as opposed to only respond or adjust to?
questions.explanation: An entrepreneur can only control the internal environment, and can only respond or adjust to changes in the external environment.

questions.text: Which of the following belong to the INTERNAL environment of a business?
questions.explanation: The internal environment is organizational structure, management support, employees, and resources. Political and legal factors are part of the external environment.

questions.text: The external environment covers Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and ___ factors.
questions.explanation: The six external factors listed are Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as personal characteristics of an entrepreneur?
options: Demanding in terms of quality and efficiency
questions.explanation: The list includes opportunity seekers, persistent, committed to work, risk-takers, demanding in terms of quality and efficiency, goal setters, information seekers, good in planning and monitoring, persuasive and good in networking, and self-confident. Persistence is the opposite of being easily discouraged.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed among the technology trends and opportunities for 2025?
questions.explanation: The 2025 list includes Generative AI, Quantum Computing, 5G expansion, Virtual Reality 2.0, Augmented Reality, Internet of Things, Biotechnology in Agriculture, Autonomous Vehicles, Blockchain, and Edge Computing.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as technology-based business ideas?
questions.explanation: The list includes website design and development, software design and development, graphic design, animation and 3D, game development, blogging, SEO, online selling, and digital shirt printing and souvenirs.

questions.text: Under "What's Next?", which three activities make up "Start Empathizing"?
questions.explanation: The closing slide lists Observe, Engage, and Immerse as the way to start empathizing.
